questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, compare AsyncSequence to standard Swift Sequence. Explain how elements are delivered and how the consuming loop knows when the sequence finishes.

rubric.criterion: Explains that AsyncSequence delivers elements asynchronously over time using for-await
Contrasts with synchronous Sequence which delivers all elements immediately
Explains that the loop terminates when next() returns nil

questions.modelAnswer: A standard Swift Sequence provides its elements immediately in memory during a synchronous loop. In contrast, an AsyncSequence delivers elements asynchronously over time, suspending the consuming task between values. The for-await loop consumes elements one by one until the iterator returns nil to signal completion.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain how AsyncStream adapts legacy callback or delegate APIs into modern concurrency. Describe the roles of yield and finish.

rubric.criterion: Explains that AsyncStream provides a continuation closure to bridge event callbacks
Explains that continuation.yield emits individual values into the stream
Explains that continuation.finish signals that no more elements will be produced

questions.modelAnswer: AsyncStream provides a continuation that bridges callback or delegate events into an async sequence. The producer calls continuation.yield(value) whenever a delegate event fires to push data into the stream buffer. When events are done, calling continuation.finish() closes the stream so the consuming for-await loop exits.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain why continuation.onTermination is essential in AsyncStream. Give an example of a resource leak that occurs without it.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains that onTermination runs when the consumer cancels or finishes iterating
Identifies that without it, producers keep running and emitting events in the background
Provides a concrete example such as CoreLocation manager or open network socket

questions.modelAnswer: continuation.onTermination is called whenever a consumer task is cancelled or stops reading the stream. Without this callback, event producers such as location managers or WebSocket connections will continue generating events in the background. Implementing onTermination allows you to stop location updates or close sockets, preventing battery drain and memory leaks.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, describe the buffering policies available in AsyncStream. Why is bufferingNewest useful for fast real-time data sources?

rubric.criterion: Identifies available policies: unbounded, bufferingNewest, and bufferingOldest
Explains that unbounded buffers can exhaust memory if consumer is slower than producer
Explains that bufferingNewest discards older stale frames, keeping fresh data and bounded memory

questions.modelAnswer: AsyncStream supports unbounded, bufferingNewest, and bufferingOldest policies. Fast producers like camera video frames can quickly exhaust memory if using the default unbounded buffer with a slow consumer. Using bufferingNewest with a fixed capacity discards older stale data, maintaining fresh sensor readings while guaranteeing bounded memory usage.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, compare AsyncSequence with Combine AnyPublisher. Mention pull versus push models and how task cancellation affects both.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains AsyncSequence is pull-based where consumer awaits values, while Combine pushes to subscribers
Explains AsyncSequence integrates natively with Swift task cancellation without AnyCancellable tokens
Explains Combine requires storing cancellable subscriptions in memory bags

questions.modelAnswer: AsyncSequence uses a pull-based model where the consumer explicitly awaits each element within a task. In contrast, Combine uses a push-based model where publishers push values to subscribers. AsyncSequence cancellation integrates directly into Swift structured concurrency, whereas Combine requires storing AnyCancellable tokens to manage subscription lifetimes.
